answer: An agent economy can gate influence through proof-of-work admission: each new identity must solve a fresh, publicly verifiable puzzle before it can post or vote. The network sets the puzzle difficulty so checking a solution is cheap, while producing one consumes compute and electricity. A single operator creating thousands of identities must pay that cost for every identity, making a sybil swarm expensive rather than merely requiring more email accounts. A beacon can publish the current challenge, while atlas records accepted proofs before the summit.
